subject: maths
question: A shopkeeper claims that he is selling rice at Rs.27/kg which cost him Rs.30/kg, but he gives 750 grams instead of 1000 grams. What is his profit or loss percentage?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net multiplier (SP/CP) = (Claimed SP ÷ Actual CP) × (True Weight ÷ Faulty Weight)

Ratio = (27 ÷ 30) × (1000 ÷ 750) = (9/10) × (4/3)

Net Ratio = 36 ÷ 30 = 6 ÷ 5

Profit % = (6 − 5) ÷ 5 × 100 = 20%

**∴ The correct answer is 20% profit.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Cost Price (CP)** of 1000 g rice = ₹30

**Selling Price (SP)** of 750 g rice (claimed as 1000 g) = ₹27

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b03f37dac48feea435079d448a0f0961354595e943d7c29ce686eec4a080f6f1.png] 

**Calculation:**

⇒ Actual **Cost Price** of 1000 g rice = ₹30

⇒ Actual **Cost Price** of 750 g rice = (30 ÷ 1000) × 750

⇒ Actual **Cost Price** of 750 g rice = ₹22.5

⇒ Given **Selling Price** of 750 g rice = ₹27

⇒ **Total Profit** = SP − CP = 27 − 22.5 = ₹4.5

⇒ **Profit Percentage** = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

⇒ **Profit Percentage** = (4.5 ÷ 22.5) × 100

⇒ **Profit Percentage** = (1 ÷ 5) × 100 = 20%

**∴ The correct answer is 20% profit.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Dishonest Dealer Concept

When a dealer sells at a profit/loss on price and also uses a **faulty weight**, the net gain/loss is calculated by the product of individual multiplication factors.

Profit with Weight Manipulation

Profit % = [(True Value − False Value) ÷ False Value] × 100. In this problem, the dealer also changed the price, so we compare the **actual CP of the weight delivered** with the **actual SP received**.

Successive Percentage Change

Net Profit % can be viewed as successive changes: price reduction (10% loss) and weight manipulation (33.33% profit). Net = −10 + 33.33 + (−10 × 33.33)/100 = 20%.
